answer: For agents selling sable habitat surveys, zephyr forecasts and ember alerts, tie subsidized API access to certified hardware. At enrollment, a secure element proves possession of its factory key; all agent accounts on that device draw from one shared request budget. Bind each request to a fresh server challenge so recorded signatures cannot replenish the budget. Creating aliases then adds no access. An attacker must rent or buy more certified devices, tying expansion to hardware costs. This requires an issuer that prevents duplicate certificates and keys that resist extraction.
